questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

# Git

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# Backlog

Reviewed at the end of slice 6, in the order I would do them. Done items are gone: the Active Suggestion no longer jumps to each new review Suggestion, and a broken answer stream has its own error text (both [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12)).

## Next

| Item | Why it waits | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Margin cards instead of the floating Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar | The toolbar covers the end of the line above its Suggestion (visible in `verification/img/5-12.png`). The maintainer approved it at Gate B; cards need their own layout, where CodeMirror tooltips already handle scroll and collisions | [#10](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/10) |
| Refine version arrows ‹ 1/3 › | The history is already kept for every step (`history`); only the UI is missing | [#11](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/11) |
| Undoable Reject (CodeMirror `invertedEffects`) | About 30 lines, but v1 accepts that a stray `Esc` loses a Suggestion. A Refine in flight or an error card already takes a first `Esc` before it Rejects | [ADR 0007](chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md), [#11](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/11) |
| Harden the Review prompt | The shipped wording passes on all 9 Bake-off models, but one sentence's position made two of them return junk Replacements. Any change needs a Bake-off re-run, about US$0.056 per full run | [#9](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/9), [bakeoff.md](chiri/bakeoff.md) |
| Junk-guard tuning | The guard drops a Replacement under 3 words for an original over 15 words (headings exempt). That covers the junk seen in the Bake-off (`x`, "Thank you!"); other shapes would pass every check | [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12), [bakeoff.md](chiri/bakeoff.md) |
| Size limit for the Review pass on huge Documents | The whole Document goes on every request: about 975 input tokens for the 331-word sample, growing in proportion. Sample-sized Documents are cheap | [ADR 0006](chiri/adr/0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md), [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12) |
| Keyboard navigation between Suggestions | Keys act on the Suggestion under the cursor, and the cards cover v1. It matters with up to 6 open Review Suggestions | [ADR 0007](chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md), [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12) |
| Rationale in the Document's language on cheaper models | `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` never slipped (0 of 9). `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` still do (6 of 9 and 3 of 9 after the ADR-faithful wording), so choosing either needs a prompt or a check first | [#9](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/9), [ADR 0006](chiri/adr/0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md) |
| Model selector in the UI | `OPENROUTER_MODEL` covers v1, and the default is the Gate A choice | [ADR 0010](chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md) |
| Draft preview for Target requests | Its reopen rule has not fired: the chosen model's median Target latency is about 2.1 s, under the ~3 s line. It fires if a slower model is chosen | [ADR 0008](chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md), [bakeoff.md](chiri/bakeoff.md) |

## Out of scope, by choice

Deploy / hosted demo · proactive AI · slash commands · split-pane before/after · chat sidebar · version history · multiple documents · real-time multi-user collaboration · mobile layout · browser end-to-end tests (the UI is checked by hand, see `chiri/verification/`).

content.content:
# Glossary

Use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues. Avoid synonyms such as "edit", "proposal" or "patch" for a Suggestion.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Document** | The Markdown text in the editor. The only thing the app persists (`localStorage`). |
| **Block** | A top-level node of the CodeMirror Markdown syntax tree: paragraph, heading, list, blockquote, code block. A whole list is one Block. |
| **Target** | The range an AI request is about: the selection, or the Block under the cursor when nothing is selected. |
| **Neighbors** | The 2 Blocks before and the 2 after the Target, plus the document title (first `#`) and the current section heading. Sent as context. |
| **Instruction** | What the user asks for: a Quick action or free text. |
| **Quick action** | A preset Instruction: Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar. |
| **Suggestion** | A proposed replacement for a range of the Document. It lives outside the Document (an overlay) until accepted. Holds: range, original text, Replacement, Rationale, refine history. |
| **Replacement** | The new text the AI proposes for a Suggestion's range. |
| **Rationale** | One short sentence from the AI explaining the change, in the Document's language. Shown on hover, or when the cursor is inside the Suggestion. |
| **Active Suggestion** | The one containing the cursor; otherwise the most recently asked Suggestion; otherwise the most important open Review pass Suggestion. The only one that shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. |
| **Accept** | Apply the Replacement to the Document. A normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. |
| **Reject** | Drop the Suggestion. Not undoable in v1. |
| **Refine** | A follow-up Instruction on an open Suggestion. Produces a new Replacement in place. The diff is always against the original text. |
| **Discard** | Remove a Suggestion because the user edited inside its range or a newer Suggestion overlapped it. Shows a discreet notice. |
| **Review pass** | On-demand request: the AI reads the whole Document (Blocks numbered `p1`, `p2`, …) and returns up to 6 Suggestions, one per Block, streamed one by one. |
| **Focus** | Optional free text that narrows a Review pass ("focus on tone"). |
| **Draft** | (Backlog) Streamed, not-yet-validated Replacement text shown without a diff. |
| **Bake-off** | Scripted comparison of candidate models on the same requests ([ADR 0010](docs/chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)). |
| **AI call record** | Per-call log entry for verification: task, model, provider, tokens, cost, timings, finish reason, generation id. |
| **Gate** | A point where the orchestrator stops for the maintainer's decision. |
----
# Implementation plan

Runbook for the implementation orchestrator. The planning session produced this plan, the [ADRs](chiri/adr/) and the issues below. Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and [GLOSSARY.md](../GLOSSARY.md) first.

## Roles

| Role | Model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `opus` | Runs the loop below, owns gates, merges PRs. Claude Code only, so every session log lands in `~/.claude/projects/`. |
| Implementer | `sonnet` subagent | One at a time, in the orchestrator's checkout, on the slice branch. |
| Reviewer, first pass | `opus` subagent, effort `medium` | Two axes, as in the `code-review` skill: **Standards** (against [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)) and **Spec** (against the issue and its ADRs). |
| Reviewer, later passes | `sonnet` subagent | Re-checks the fixes until no real findings remain. |

Slices run **sequentially**. Each builds on the previous one, and running them in parallel would collide on `package.json` and shared modules.

## Loop per slice

1. Branch from up-to-date `main`, using the name in the table below.
2. Implementer: TDD the pure modules the issue lists, then the UI.
3. Run the definition of done ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#definition-of-done-every-slice)): tests, Biome, build.
4. Verify the acceptance criteria in a real browser with `agent-browser`. Record the AI calls and screenshots ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#ai-call-records)) and update [chiri/ai-costs.md](chiri/ai-costs.md).
5. Open the PR with the `pr` skill and the [template](../.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).
6. First review (`opus`, medium), fix, then re-review (`sonnet`) until clean. Note the review outcome in the PR.
7. Squash merge.
8. If the slice ends at a gate, stop and wait.

## Slices

| # | Issue | Branch | Scope | Depends on | Gate after | Est. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [#1](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/1) | `feat/editor-shell` | Vite + React + TS + Tailwind, CodeMirror with styled Markdown, sample Document, `localStorage`, proxy, missing-key banner, Biome, Vitest | — | — | 45 min |
| 2 | [#2](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/2) | `feat/model-client-bakeoff` | AI SDK client, zod schemas, prompt building, Block extraction, AI call records, `scripts/bakeoff.ts`, `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md` | 1 | **A** | 60 min |
| 3 | [#3](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/3) | `feat/selection-suggestions` | Selection bubble, `Cmd+K`, Quick actions, Suggestion state and mapping, adaptive diff, overlay decorations, Accept / Reject, Rationale, errors | 2, Gate A | **B** | 90 min |
| 4 | [#4](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/4) | `feat/refine` | Refine on the Active Suggestion, history, diff against original | 3, Gate B | — | 30 min |
| 5 | [#5](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/5) | `feat/review-pass` | Review pass with Focus, numbered Blocks, streamed validated Suggestions (max 6), skip occupied Blocks, Accept all / Reject all | 4 | — | 45 min |
| 6 | [#6](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/6) | `docs/readme-and-sessions` | Final README, backlog review, session export script, `ai-sessions/` | 5 | **C** | 30 min |

That is about 5 h 15 of work, plus 30–40 min of reviews. If time runs short, shrink slice 5 first.

## Gates

- **A, after slice 2 (model):** present `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`, with outputs side by side, latency, cost and validity. The maintainer picks the model or models. Update [ADR 0010](chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md) to Accepted and set the default in `.env.example`. If any Target-request latency is above ~3 s, flag the Draft reopen rule ([ADR 0008](chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md)).
- **B, after slice 3 (core flow):** the maintainer tries select → Suggestion → Accept / Reject in the browser. Fix taste issues before Refine and the Review pass build on top.
- **C, before merging slice 6 (submission):** final look at the README, cost log, sessions and repo.

## Budget

US$5 OpenRouter cap. The Bake-off should stay under US$0.50. Every model call made during verification goes into [chiri/ai-costs.md](chiri/ai-costs.md). If the running total passes US$2, stop and tell the maintainer.

## Session logs (slice 6)

The challenge requires raw, unedited session files committed to the repo. Only secrets may be masked.

- Source: every folder in `~/.claude/projects/` whose name starts with `-home-walter-Github-chiri-ai-editor` (this covers every worktree). Copy each session's `<id>.jsonl` and its sibling `<id>/` folder (subagents, tool results) as they are. Skip non-session files such as `memory/`.
- Destination: `ai-sessions/<project-folder>/…`.
- Masking: replace OpenRouter keys (`sk-or-…`) with `sk-or-***MASKED***`, and nothing else.
- The script lives in `scripts/` and runs last, after the final PR text is written, so it captures as much as possible. Note in the README that the orchestrator session continues after the export.
- Claude Code deletes transcripts older than `cleanupPeriodDays`, 30 days by default. Export before then.
----

{"body":"No linked issue: maintainer requests from a review session.

## Summary

Chiri palette (from chiri.ai CSS tokens), flat UI, and three editor fixes found while using it.

```text
src/index.css             # 3 surfaces · ink at 4 alphas · orange #E37545 · danger; tints derived
src/editor/suggestions.css # no borders, no radius; orange outline only on :focus-visible
```

```diff
 .cm-codeblock-line
-  padding: 0 0.75rem                       # CodeMirror reads the first rendered .cm-line's padding for every selection rect
+  border-inline: 0.75rem solid transparent
```

```diff
 Tab in editor
+  Ask bubble or Active Suggestion card open → focus its first item (Shift+Tab: last)
 Tab inside bubble / card
-  last item → leaves the app
+  last item → first item (cycleIndex)
+ Esc on a bubble button → dismiss, back to text · on a card button → back to text (no Reject)
```

```diff
 bubble placement
-  above Target start                       # scrolled out while extending down
+  selection empty → above Target start
+  else            → at the cursor (head), above when extending up, below when extending down
 scroll into view
+  EditorView.scrollMargins top = sticky header height     # caret never lands under the header
 tooltip (bubble, Active Suggestion card)
+  clip: false, z-index 20 < header z-30                    # CodeMirror's clip check assumes the editor scrolls itself; the page does
```

Deviations:
- Diff colors leave the red/green convention: deleted is faint struck-through ink, inserted is light orange.
- Missing-key banner is neutral instead of amber.
- Code background stays translucent (white 5%): CodeMirror draws the selection behind line backgrounds, so an opaque one hides it.
- `tooltipSpaceBelow` → `spaceBelowHeader` (now also sets scroll margins).

15	import { cycleTab } from './focus-cycle'

34	type CardContent = {
35	  readonly suggestion: ReadySuggestion
36	  readonly showRationale: boolean
37	  readonly showActions: boolean
38	  readonly refineOpen: boolean
39	}
40	
41	type CardKind = 'active' | 'hover'
42	
43	const contentFor = (
44	  kind: CardKind,
45	  state: EditorState,
46	): CardContent | undefined => {
47	  const hoveredId = state.field(interactionField).hoveredId
48	  const active = activeOf(state)
49	  if (kind === 'active') {
50	    if (!active) return undefined
51	    const cursorInside =
52	      active.from <= cursorOf(state) && cursorOf(state) <= active.to
53	    return {
54	      suggestion: active,
55	      showRationale: cursorInside || hoveredId === active.id,
56	      showActions: true,
57	      refineOpen: refineInputOpenFor(state) === active.id,
58	    }
59	  }
60	  if (hoveredId === null || hoveredId === active?.id) return undefined
61	  const hovered = findSuggestion(suggestionsOf(state), hoveredId)
62	  return hovered?.status === 'ready'
63	    ? {
64	        suggestion: hovered,
65	        showRationale: true,
66	        showActions: false,
67	        refineOpen: false,
68	      }
69	    : undefined
70	}
71	
72	const refineKey = ({ refine }: ReadySuggestion): string =>
73	  refine.status === 'failed'
74	    ? `failed:${describeError(refine.error)}`
75	    : refine.status
76	
77	const contentKey = ({
78	  suggestion,
79	  showRationale,
80	  showActions,
81	  refineOpen,
82	}: CardContent): string =>
83	  [
84	    suggestion.id,
85	    suggestion.rationale,
86	    showRationale,
87	    showActions,
88	    refineOpen,
89	    refineKey(suggestion),
90	  ].join('\u0000')
91	
92	const shortcutLabel = (key: string): string =>
93	  formatShortcut(key, detectApplePlatform())
94	
95	type ButtonOptions = {
96	  readonly refocus?: boolean
97	  readonly disabled?: boolean
98	  readonly busy?: boolean
99	  readonly expanded?: boolean
100	}
101	
102	const actionButton = (
103	  view: EditorView,
104	  label: string,
105	  hint: string | undefined,
106	  run: () => void,
107	  {
108	    refocus = true,
109	    disabled = false,
110	    busy = false,
111	    expanded,
112	  }: ButtonOptions = {},
113	) =>
114	  el(
115	    'button',
116	    {
117	      class: 'cm-ai-button',
118	      attrs: {
119	        type: 'button',

121	        ...(busy && { 'aria-busy': 'true' }),

161	          event.preventDefault()

163	      },
164	    },
165	  })

171	        submit: (event) => {
172	          event.preventDefault()

181	        },
182	      },
183	    },
184	    [input],

189	const refineButton = (
190	  view: EditorView,
191	  { suggestion, refineOpen }: CardContent,
192	) =>

232	      ]
233	    : []
234	
235	const renderCard = (
236	  view: EditorView,
237	  content: CardContent,
238	  { form }: RefineForm,
239	): Node[] => {
240	  const { suggestion, showRationale, showActions, refineOpen } = content

# 0001. Inline Suggestions as an overlay on a raw-Markdown CodeMirror editor

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q1, Q2, Q9

## Context

The challenge asks for visible diffs before the user accepts, and for an experience that feels like a co-author, "not a chatbot in a sidebar". We had to choose where Suggestions appear and what kind of editor holds the text.

## Decision

- **Editor:** CodeMirror 6 showing raw Markdown with light styling, Obsidian-like: bigger headings, bold looks bold, syntax marks stay visible.
- **Suggestions inline, as tracked changes:** deleted text is struck through in place and the Replacement shows next to it, rendered with CodeMirror decorations and widgets.
- **Overlay, not content:** Suggestions live in editor state outside the Document. The Document only ever holds the user's text. Accept applies the Replacement as a normal edit. Reject drops the Suggestion.

## Consequences

- The Document is a plain string, so diffs are plain string diffs: simple and reliable.
- Copying, saving and persisting never leak Suggestion markup.
- The Replacement is not directly editable. Users Refine it, or Accept and then edit.
- Less "Google Docs" polish than a WYSIWYG editor.

## Alternatives considered

- **Split pane before/after:** easier, but the eye jumps between two places and it feels like a tool, not a partner.
- **Chat sidebar producing patches:** what the challenge says to avoid.
- **Tiptap / ProseMirror WYSIWYG:** the Markdown round-trip is lossy, and tracked changes over a node tree are notoriously hard.
- **Suggestion text inserted into the Document with marks:** the Markdown stays dirty while Suggestions are open, and Reject needs careful undo.
# 0007. Suggestion lifecycle

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q13, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q25, Q32

## Context

Suggestions are overlays ([0001](0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md)) and the user keeps typing while they are open or in flight.

## Decision

- **Edits outside a Suggestion:** its range is mapped through the change (CodeMirror `ChangeSet` mapping).
- **Edits inside an open Suggestion, or inside an in-flight request's Target:** Discard it, with a discreet notice ("Suggestion discarded: the text changed").
- **Overlaps:** a new request over an open Suggestion replaces it, so the last one wins. The Review pass skips Blocks with open Suggestions.
- **Active Suggestion:** shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. Its Rationale shows on hover, and when the text cursor is inside it (keyboard users can't hover). Other Suggestions show only the inline diff.
- **Keys, with the cursor inside a Suggestion:** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` Accepts, `Esc` Rejects. Accept is a normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. Reject is not undoable in v1. A Review pass also offers Accept all and Reject all.
- **Refine:** a follow-up Instruction on the Active Suggestion. The new Replacement replaces the old one in place. The diff is always against the original text. History stays in memory, with no version arrows in v1.
- **Persistence:** only the Document text goes to `localStorage`. Open Suggestions are lost on reload.
- **Failures:**
  - Missing key: banner ([0005](0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
  - Failed call (network, `402` out of credit, `429`): the Suggestion becomes an error card with Retry. `402` gets its own message.
  - Invalid output: one silent retry, then the error card.
  - Timeout: 30 s.

## Consequences

- Simple, honest rules. A user who bumps into a Suggestion loses it, and can ask again.
- An accidental `Esc` loses a Suggestion. An undoable Reject is in the backlog.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep a stale Suggestion with "regenerate":** an extra state, and an old diff can't be drawn over changed text.
- **Lock the range while a Suggestion is open:** takes control away from the user.
- **Block new requests until the old Suggestion is resolved:** friction.
- **Allow overlapping Suggestions:** accepting one breaks the other.
- **Rationale always visible, or in a side panel:** the side panel drifts toward the chatbot sidebar.

# Architecture decisions

All decisions were made in the planning session (see `ai-sessions/`), with question numbers (Qn) cited in each ADR.

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md) | Inline Suggestions as an overlay on a raw-Markdown CodeMirror editor | Accepted |
| [0002](0002-structured-output-app-owned-anchors.md) | Structured model output; the app owns the anchors | Accepted |
| [0003](0003-adaptive-diff.md) | Adaptive diff granularity | Accepted |
| [0004](0004-user-triggered-ai-and-review-pass.md) | User-triggered AI, plus an on-demand Review pass | Accepted |
| [0005](0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md) | Local-only app; API key behind the Vite dev proxy | Accepted |
| [0006](0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md) | Context window and prompt rules | Accepted |
| [0007](0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md) | Suggestion lifecycle | Accepted |
| [0008](0008-validated-streaming-only.md) | Stream only where each piece arrives validated | Accepted |
| [0009](0009-ai-sdk-v7.md) | AI SDK v7 instead of plain fetch | Accepted |
| [0010](0010-model-bakeoff.md) | Choose the model by Bake-off | Accepted |

Process decisions (slices, roles, gates, reviews) live in [docs/PLAN.md](../../PLAN.md).
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `⌘K` | Ask about the selection, or the paragraph under the cursor. Inside a Suggestion: Refine it. |
| `⌘Enter` | Accept the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `Esc` | Close the bubble or the Refine box; cancel a request or a Refine in flight; otherwise Reject the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `⌘Z` | Undo an Accept, or an Accept all in one step. Reject cannot be undone. |

## With more time

Details and sources in [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md).

1. **Margin cards instead of the floating toolbar.** The toolbar can cover the end of the line above the Suggestion (visible in the screenshot).
2. **Version arrows for Refine** (‹ 1/3 ›). Every Refine step is already kept; only the UI is missing.
3. **Undoable Reject.** One stray `Esc` loses a Suggestion for good.
4. **A sturdier Review prompt.** In the Bake-off, moving one sentence made two models return junk Replacements. A guard drops the one shape seen so far, and the prompt still needs a Bake-off re-run after any change.
5. **A size limit for the Review pass.** It sends the whole Document, so cost and latency grow with it and nothing stops a very long one.

## Links

- [Architecture decisions](docs/chiri/adr/) (10 ADRs), [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), [plan](docs/PLAN.md)
- [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md): all 9 models side by side
- [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md): US$0.269 of 5.00 spent
- [Verification records](docs/chiri/verification/): one per slice, with screenshots and the AI call tables
- [The challenge](docs/chiri/CHALLENGE.md)
- [`ai-sessions/`](ai-sessions/): the raw Claude Code `.jsonl` files, as saved. Only OpenRouter keys are masked (`sk-or-***MASKED***`); nothing else is edited. The planning session is in the `grilling` folder. The orchestrator session is in the `chiri-implementation-orchestration` folder, and its implementer and reviewer subagents are under `<session id>/subagents/`. The orchestrator session continues after the export, so its last turns (Gate C and the merge) are not in it.

import { EditorState, type TransactionSpec } from '@codemirror/state'

  closeRefineEffect,

} from './refine-input'
import type { EditorHandle } from './suggestion-commands'
import {
  beginEffect,
  beginRefineEffect,
  failRefineEffect,
  rejectEffect,
  resolveEffect,
  suggestionsField,
} from './suggestion-field'

const DOC = 'First paragraph here.\n\nSecond paragraph here.'

const createHandle = (anchor = 5): EditorHandle => {
  let state = EditorState.create({
    doc: DOC,
    selection: { anchor },
    extensions: [suggestionsField, refineInputField],
  })
  return {
    get state() {
      return state
    },
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { spaceBelow } from './tooltip-space'

describe('spaceBelow', () => {
  it('starts the space under the inset and keeps the rest of the viewport', () => {
    expect(spaceBelow(72, { width: 1200, height: 900 })).toEqual({
      top: 72,
      left: 0,
      right: 1200,
      bottom: 900,
    })
  })

  it('never starts above the viewport', () => {
    expect(spaceBelow(-30, { width: 800, height: 600 }).top).toBe(0)
  })
})

# agent-browser

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP with
accessibility-tree snapshots and compact `@eN` element refs.

Install: `npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install`

## Start here

This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide. Before running any
`agent-browser` command, load the actual workflow content from the CLI:

```bash
agent-browser skills get core             # start here — workflows, common patterns, troubleshooting
agent-browser skills get core --full      # include full command reference and templates
```

The CLI serves skill content that always matches the installed version,
so instructions never go stale. The content in this stub cannot change
between releases, which is why it just points at `skills get core`.

## Specialized skills

Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser web pages:

```bash
agent-browser skills get electron          # Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, ...)
agent-browser skills get slack             # Slack workspace automation
agent-browser skills get dogfood           # Exploratory testing / QA / bug hunts
agent-browser skills get vercel-sandbox    # agent-browser inside Vercel Sandbox microVMs
agent-browser skills get agentcore         # AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers
```

Run `agent-browser skills list` to see everything available on the
installed version.

## Why agent-browser

- Fast native Rust CLI, not a Node.js wrapper
- Works with any AI agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Continue, Windsurf, etc.)
- Chrome/Chromium via CDP with no Playwright or Puppeteer dependency
- Accessibility-tree snapshots with element refs for reliable interaction
- Sessions, authentication vault, state persistence, video recording
- Specialized skills for Electron apps, Slack, exploratory testing, cloud providers

## Observability Dashboard

The dashboard runs independently of browser sessions on port 4848 and can also be opened through a proxied or forwarded URL such as `https://dashboard.agent-browser.localhost`. Agents should stay on the dashboard origin: session tabs, status, and stream traffic are proxied internally, so session ports do not need to be exposed.

---
name: core
description: Core agent-browser usage guide. Read this before running any agent-browser commands. Covers the snapshot-and-ref workflow, navigating pages, interacting with elements (click, fill, type, select), extracting text and data, taking screenshots, managing tabs, handling forms and auth, waiting for content, running multiple browser sessions in parallel, and troubleshooting common failures. Use when the user asks to interact with a website, fill a form, click something, extract data, take a screenshot, log into a site, test a web app, or automate any browser task.
allowed-tools: Bash(agent-browser:*), Bash(npx agent-browser:*)
---

# agent-browser core

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no
Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact
`@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of
parsing raw HTML.

Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are
covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser
web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).

## The core loop

```bash
agent-browser open <url>        # 1. Open a page
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 2. See what's on it (interactive elements only)
agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
```

Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become
**stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form
submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your
next ref interaction.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Install once
npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install

# Take a screenshot of a page
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser screenshot home.png
agent-browser close

# Search, click a result, and capture it
agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
agent-browser press Enter
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
agent-browser screenshot result.png
```

The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single
session. Use `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.

## Reading a page

```bash
agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
```

Snapshot output looks like:

```
Page: Example - Log in
URL: https://example.com/login

@e1 [heading] "Log in"
@e2 [form]
  @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
  @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
  @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
  @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
```

For unstructured reading (no refs needed):

```bash
agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
agent-browser get title                   # page title
agent-browser get url                     # current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
```

## Interacting

```bash
agent-browser click @e1                   # click
agent-browser click @e1 --new-tab         # open link in new tab instead of navigating
agent-browser dblclick @e1                # double-click
agent-browser hover @e1                   # hover
agent-browser focus @e1                   # focus (useful before keyboard input)
agent-browser fill @e2 "hello"            # clear then type
agent-browser type @e2 " world"           # type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter                 # press a key at current focus
agent-browser press Control+a             # key combination
agent-browser check @e3                   # check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e3                 # uncheck
agent-browser select @e4 "option-value"   # select dropdown option
agent-browser select @e4 "a" "b"          # select multiple
agent-browser upload @e5 file1.pdf        # upload file(s)
agent-browser scroll down 500             # scroll page (up/down/left/right)
agent-browser scrollintoview @e1          # scroll element into view
agent-browser drag @e1 @e2                # drag and drop
```

### When refs don't work or you don't want to snapshot

Use semantic locators:

```bash
agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click --exact     # exact match only
agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
agent-browser find placeholder "Search" type "query"
agent-browser find testid "submit-btn" click
agent-browser find first ".card" click
agent-browser find nth 2 ".card" hover
```

Or a raw CSS selector:

```bash
agent-browser click "#submit"
agent-browser fill "input[name=email]" "user@test.com"
agent-browser click "button.primary"
```

Rule of thumb: snapshot + `@eN` refs are fastest and most reliable for
AI agents. `find role/text/label` is next best and doesn't require a prior
snapshot. Raw CSS is a fallback when the others fail.

## Waiting (read this)

Agents fail more often from bad waits than from bad selectors. Pick the
right wait for the situation:

```bash
agent-browser wait @e1                     # until an element appears

agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
```

Snapshot output looks like:

```
Page: Example - Log in
URL: https://example.com/login

@e1 [heading] "Log in"
@e2 [form]
  @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
  @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
  @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
  @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
```

For unstructured reading (no refs needed):

```bash
agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
agent-browser get title                   # page title
agent-browser get url                     # current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
```

## Interacting

```bash
agent-browser click @e1                   # click
agent-browser click @e1 --new-tab         # open link in new tab instead of navigating
agent-browser dblclick @e1                # double-click
agent-browser hover @e1                   # hover
agent-browser focus @e1                   # focus (useful before keyboard input)
agent-browser fill @e2 "hello"            # clear then type
agent-browser type @e2 " world"           # type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter                 # press a key at current focus
agent-browser press Control+a             # key combination
agent-browser check @e3                   # check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e3                 # uncheck
agent-browser select @e4 "option-value"   # select dropdown option
agent-browser select @e4 "a" "b"          # select multiple
agent-browser upload @e5 file1.pdf        # upload file(s)
agent-browser scroll down 500             # scroll page (up/down/left/right)
agent-browser scrollintoview @e1          # scroll element into view
agent-browser drag @e1 @e2                # drag and drop
```

### When refs don't work or you don't want to snapshot

Use semantic locators:

```bash
agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click --exact     # exact match only
agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
agent-browser find placeholder "Search" type "query"
agent-browser find testid "submit-btn" click
agent-browser find first ".card" click
agent-browser find nth 2 ".card" hover
```

Or a raw CSS selector:

```bash
agent-browser click "#submit"
agent-browser fill "input[name=email]" "user@test.com"
agent-browser click "button.primary"
```

Rule of thumb: snapshot + `@eN` refs are fastest and most reliable for
AI agents. `find role/text/label` is next best and doesn't require a prior
snapshot. Raw CSS is a fallback when the others fail.

## Waiting (read this)

Agents fail more often from bad waits than from bad selectors. Pick the
right wait for the situation:

```bash
agent-browser wait @e1                     # until an element appears

# Chiri AI Editor

## What it is

A browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. Select text, or put the cursor in a paragraph, and ask for a change with a Quick action (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar), free text, or `⌘K`. The AI answers inline as a tracked change: the old text struck through, the new text beside it, and a one-line Rationale on hover. Small edits show a word-level diff; rewrites show the whole block. # Glossary

Use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues. Avoid synonyms such as "edit", "proposal" or "patch" for a Suggestion.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Document** | The Markdown text in the editor. The only thing the app persists (`localStorage`). |
| **Block** | A top-level node of the CodeMirror Markdown syntax tree: paragraph, heading, list, blockquote, code block. A whole list is one Block. |
| **Target** | The range an AI request is about: the selection, or the Block under the cursor when nothing is selected. |
| **Neighbors** | The 2 Blocks before and the 2 after the Target, plus the document title (first `#`) and the current section heading. Sent as context. |
| **Instruction** | What the user asks for: a Quick action or free text. |
| **Quick action** | A preset Instruction: Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar. |
| **Suggestion** | A proposed replacement for a range of the Document. It lives outside the Document (an overlay) until accepted. Holds: range, original text, Replacement, Rationale, refine history. |
| **Replacement** | The new text the AI proposes for a Suggestion's range. |
| **Rationale** | One short sentence from the AI explaining the change, in the Document's language. Shown on hover, or when the cursor is inside the Suggestion. |
| **Active Suggestion** | The one containing the cursor; otherwise the most recently asked Suggestion; otherwise the most important open Review pass Suggestion. The only one that shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. |
| **Accept** | Apply the Replacement to the Document. A normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. |
| **Reject** | Drop the Suggestion. Not undoable in v1. |
| **Refine** | A follow-up Instruction on an open Suggestion. Produces a new Replacement in place. The diff is always against the original text. |
| **Discard** | Remove a Suggestion because the user edited inside its range or a newer Suggestion overlapped it. Shows a discreet notice. |
| **Review pass** | On-demand request: the AI reads the whole Document (Blocks numbered `p1`, `p2`, …) and returns up to 6 Suggestions, one per Block, streamed one by one. |
| **Focus** | Optional free text that narrows a Review pass ("focus on tone"). |
| **Draft** | (Backlog) Streamed, not-yet-validated Replacement text shown without a diff. |
| **Bake-off** | Scripted comparison of candidate models on the same requests ([ADR 0010](docs/chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)). |
| **AI call record** | Per-call log entry for verification: task, model, provider, tokens, cost, timings, finish reason, generation id. |
| **Gate** | A point where the orchestrator stops for the maintainer's decision. |

# Glossary

Use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues. Avoid synonyms such as "edit", "proposal" or "patch" for a Suggestion.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Document** | The Markdown text in the editor. The only thing the app persists (`localStorage`). |
| **Block** | A top-level node of the CodeMirror Markdown syntax tree: paragraph, heading, list, blockquote, code block. A whole list is one Block. |
| **Target** | The range an AI request is about: the selection, or the Block under the cursor when nothing is selected. |
| **Neighbors** | The 2 Blocks before and the 2 after the Target, plus the document title (first `#`) and the current section heading. Sent as context. |
| **Instruction** | What the user asks for: a Quick action or free text. |
| **Quick action** | A preset Instruction: Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar. |
| **Suggestion** | A proposed replacement for a range of the Document. It lives outside the Document (an overlay) until accepted. Holds: range, original text, Replacement, Rationale, refine history. |
| **Replacement** | The new text the AI proposes for a Suggestion's range. |
| **Rationale** | One short sentence from the AI explaining the change, in the Document's language. Shown on hover, or when the cursor is inside the Suggestion. |
| **Active Suggestion** | The one containing the cursor; otherwise the most recently asked Suggestion; otherwise the most important open Review pass Suggestion. The only one that shows the Accept / Reject / Refine card: in the right margin, level with its first line, when the window has room; otherwise floating above it. |
| **Accept** | Apply the Replacement to the Document. A normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. |
| **Reject** | Drop the Suggestion. Not undoable in v1. |
| **Refine** | A follow-up Instruction on an open Suggestion. Produces a new Replacement in place. The diff is always against the original text. |
| **Discard** | Remove a Suggestion because the user edited inside its range or a newer Suggestion overlapped it. Shows a discreet notice. |
| **Review pass** | On-demand request: the AI reads the whole Document (Blocks numbered `p1`, `p2`, …) and returns up to 6 Suggestions, one per Block, streamed one by one. |
| **Focus** | Optional free text that narrows a Review pass ("focus on tone"). |
| **Draft** | (Backlog) Streamed, not-yet-validated Replacement text shown without a diff. |
| **Bake-off** | Scripted comparison of candidate models on the same requests ([ADR 0010](docs/chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)). |
| **AI call record** | Per-call log entry for verification: task, model, provider, tokens, cost, timings, finish reason, generation id. |
| **Gate** | A point where the orchestrator stops for the maintainer's decision. |

# 0007. Suggestion lifecycle

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q13, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q25, Q32

## Context

Suggestions are overlays ([0001](0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md)) and the user keeps typing while they are open or in flight.

## Decision

- **Edits outside a Suggestion:** its range is mapped through the change (CodeMirror `ChangeSet` mapping).
- **Edits inside an open Suggestion, or inside an in-flight request's Target:** Discard it, with a discreet notice ("Suggestion discarded: the text changed").
- **Overlaps:** a new request over an open Suggestion replaces it, so the last one wins. The Review pass skips Blocks with open Suggestions.
- **Active Suggestion:** shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. Its Rationale shows on hover, and when the text cursor is inside it (keyboard users can't hover). Other Suggestions show only the inline diff.
- **Keys, with the cursor inside a Suggestion:** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` Accepts, `Esc` Rejects. Accept is a normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. Reject is not undoable in v1. A Review pass also offers Accept all and Reject all.
- **Refine:** a follow-up Instruction on the Active Suggestion. The new Replacement replaces the old one in place. The diff is always against the original text. History stays in memory, with no version arrows in v1.
- **Persistence:** only the Document text goes to `localStorage`. Open Suggestions are lost on reload.
- **Failures:**
  - Missing key: banner ([0005](0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
  - Failed call (network, `402` out of credit, `429`): the Suggestion becomes an error card with Retry. `402` gets its own message.
  - Invalid output: one silent retry, then the error card.
  - Timeout: 30 s.

## Consequences

- Simple, honest rules. A user who bumps into a Suggestion loses it, and can ask again.
- An accidental `Esc` loses a Suggestion. An undoable Reject is in the backlog.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep a stale Suggestion with "regenerate":** an extra state, and an old diff can't be drawn over changed text.
- **Lock the range while a Suggestion is open:** takes control away from the user.
- **Block new requests until the old Suggestion is resolved:** friction.
- **Allow overlapping Suggestions:** accepting one breaks the other.
- **Rationale always visible, or in a side panel:** the side panel drifts toward the chatbot sidebar.

# Backlog

Reviewed at the end of slice 6, in the order I would do them. Done items are gone: the Active Suggestion no longer jumps to each new review Suggestion, and a broken answer stream has its own error text (both [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12)).

The maintainer approved it at Gate B; cards need their own layout, where CodeMirror tooltips already handle scroll and collisions | [#10](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/10) |
| Refine version arrows ‹ 1/3 › | The history is already kept for every step (`history`); only the UI is missing | [#11](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/11) |

# Chiri AI Editor

## What it is

A browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. Select text, or put the cursor in a paragraph, and ask for a change with a Quick action (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar), free text, or `⌘K`. The AI answers inline as a tracked change: the old text struck through, the new text beside it, and a one-line Rationale on hover. Small edits show a word-level diff; rewrites show the whole block. You can Accept, Reject, or Refine a Suggestion ("make it shorter", then "now more formal"). A Review pass reads the whole Document, optionally with a Focus ("tone only"), and streams up to six Suggestions, with Accept all and Reject all. Nothing touches the Document until you Accept, and Accept is a normal edit, so `⌘Z` undoes it.

![Review pass with the Focus "tone only": two word-level Suggestions and one block-level, with the toolbar on the active one](docs/chiri/verification/img/5-12.png)

**How it was built.**
- A planning session (Claude Code, `grilling` skill) produced the [ADRs](docs/chiri/adr/), the [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), the [plan](docs/PLAN.md) and six issues.
- An orchestrator session (Claude Code, `opus`) ran the six slices one after another. Each slice had a `sonnet` implementer subagent (tests first for the pure modules, then the UI), a check of the acceptance criteria in a real browser, and a review by `opus` (Standards and Spec) followed by `sonnet` until clean. The maintainer decided at three gates: the model (A), the core flow (B) and this submission (C).
- The default model, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, was chosen by a [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md) of 9 models on the same requests (final run US$0.056; about US$0.17 for the three full runs plus the language re-check; about US$0.23 for everything spent on choosing the model, with the prompt checks and probes).
- Every model call made while building was recorded against the US$5 budget in the [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md). The UI has no end-to-end suite; it was checked by hand, and each check is written up in [docs/chiri/verification/](docs/chiri/verification/).

## How to run it

Needs Node 22.12 or newer and pnpm (the version is pinned in `packageManager`; `corepack enable` installs it).

```sh
cp .env.example .env     # then set OPENROUTER_API_KEY
pnpm install
pnpm dev                 # open the printed URL
```

- `OPENROUTER_MODEL` is optional and defaults to `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`.
- The key stays on the server side. The browser sends a placeholder, and the Vite proxy (`/api/openrouter/*`) overwrites `Authorization`. `.env` is not committed and the built bundle contains no key ([ADR 0005](docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)). The app is local only; there is no hosted version.
- Without a key the app opens and shows a banner that says what is missing.
- To try it: the sample Document has an overlong paragraph, a slangy one and a typo. Select one and press `⌘K`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | Vitest. Never calls the model. |
| `pnpm biome check` | Lint and format. |
| `pnpm build` | Type-check and production build. |

# Chiri AI Editor

## What it is

A browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. Select text, or put the cursor in a paragraph, and ask for a change with a Quick action (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar), free text, or `⌘K`. The AI answers inline as a tracked change: the old text struck through, the new text beside it, and a one-line Rationale on hover. Small edits show a word-level diff; rewrites show the whole block. You can Accept, Reject, or Refine a Suggestion ("make it shorter", then "now more formal"). A Review pass reads the whole Document, optionally with a Focus ("tone only"), and streams up to six Suggestions, with Accept all and Reject all. Nothing touches the Document until you Accept, and Accept is a normal edit, so `⌘Z` undoes it.

![Review pass with the Focus "tone only": two word-level Suggestions and one block-level, with the toolbar on the active one](docs/chiri/verification/img/5-12.png)

**How it was built.**
- A planning session (Claude Code, `grilling` skill) produced the [ADRs](docs/chiri/adr/), the [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), the [plan](docs/PLAN.md) and six issues.
- An orchestrator session (Claude Code, `opus`) ran the six slices one after another. Each slice had a `sonnet` implementer subagent (tests first for the pure modules, then the UI), a check of the acceptance criteria in a real browser, and a review by `opus` (Standards and Spec) followed by `sonnet` until clean. The maintainer decided at three gates: the model (A), the core flow (B) and this submission (C).
- The default model, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, was chosen by a [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md) of 9 models on the same requests (final run US$0.056; about US$0.17 for the three full runs plus the language re-check; about US$0.23 for everything spent on choosing the model, with the prompt checks and probes).
- Every model call made while building was recorded against the US$5 budget in the [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md). The UI has no end-to-end suite; it was checked by hand, and each check is written up in [docs/chiri/verification/](docs/chiri/verification/).

## How to run it

Needs Node 22.12 or newer and pnpm (the version is pinned in `packageManager`; `corepack enable` installs it).

```sh
cp .env.example .env     # then set OPENROUTER_API_KEY
pnpm install
pnpm dev                 # open the printed URL
```

- `OPENROUTER_MODEL` is optional and defaults to `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`.
- The key stays on the server side. The browser sends a placeholder, and the Vite proxy (`/api/openrouter/*`) overwrites `Authorization`. `.env` is not committed and the built bundle contains no key ([ADR 0005](docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)). The app is local only; there is no hosted version.
- Without a key the app opens and shows a banner that says what is missing.
- To try it: the sample Document has an overlong paragraph, a slangy one and a typo. Select one and press `⌘K`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | Vitest. Never calls the model. |
| `pnpm biome check` | Lint and format. |
| `pnpm build` | Type-check and production build. |
| `pnpm bakeoff` | Calls the model: 9 models, 4 Quick actions and a Review pass each, about US$0.056. Rewrites `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`. Needs the key. |
| `pnpm export-sessions` | Copies the Claude Code sessions into `ai-sessions/` with OpenRouter keys masked. `--verify` compares the copy with the source. |

Keys (`Ctrl` instead of `⌘` outside macOS):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `⌘K` | Ask about the selection, or the paragraph under the cursor. Inside a Suggestion: Refine it. |
| `⌘Enter` | Accept the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `Esc` | Close the bubble or the Refine box; cancel a request or a Refine in flight; otherwise Reject the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `⌘Z` | Undo an Accept, or an Accept all in one step. Reject cannot be undone. |

## With more time

Details and sources in [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md).

1. **Version arrows for Refine** (‹ 1/3 ›). Every Refine step is already kept; only the UI is missing.
2. **Undoable Reject.** One stray `Esc` loses a Suggestion for good.
