content.text:
Pronto: o primeiro item do backlog, **margin cards**, está feito no branch `feat/margin-cards`. Ainda não fiz commit.

**O que mudou na tela**
- Quando a página tem espaço à direita do texto, o cartão Accept / Reject / Refine da Active Suggestion fica na margem. Ele começa na mesma altura da primeira linha da Suggestion e não cobre mais o texto.
- Nesse modo, o Rationale aparece sempre. Levar o mouse do texto até o botão não muda o cartão: medi altura 115.9 e topo 640.9 o tempo todo.
- As outras Suggestions mostram o Rationale num cartão sem botões, no hover, também na margem. Se dois cartões se encostam, o de hover desce para baixo do Active.
- Janela estreita: volta o balão flutuante de hoje, com o defeito de hoje.

**Como funciona por dentro**
- [card-placement.ts](src/editor/card-placement.ts) é novo. Um campo de estado guarda o modo (`margin` ou `floating`), e um plugin escuta o resize da janela para trocar o modo.
- Em [suggestion-cards.ts](src/editor/suggestion-cards.ts), o cartão no modo `margin` diz ao CodeMirror onde ficar, por `getCoords`. Cada modo tem sua própria função `create`. Assim o CodeMirror monta um balão novo quando o modo troca, em vez de lembrar o lado (cima/baixo) do modo antigo.

**Verificado**
- `pnpm test`: 40 arquivos, 640 testes passando, com 15 testes novos.
- `pnpm biome check`: sem avisos. `pnpm build`: verde.
- Browser (agent-browser), com Suggestions injetadas sem chamar o modelo, então custo US$0:
  - alinhamento com a linha;
  - hover;
  - troca de Active;
  - Tab dentro do cartão e Esc;
  - Ctrl+K para o Refine;
  - Accept pelo clique;
  - scroll;
  - resize de 1440 para 1280 e de volta.
- Os prints estão em `docs/chiri/verification/img/margin-cards-1.png` até `-4.png`.

**Onde você pode discordar**
- O limite real é a área útil da página com ≥1312px, o que dá uma janela de uns 1328px contando a barra de rolagem. Em 1280px o cartão continua flutuando.
- A folga entre dois cartões empilhados é de 2px. Esse número vem do próprio CodeMirror e não dá para mudar sem reescrever o posicionamento dele.
- Mudei o texto do ADR 0007 e do Glossary para "card", e marquei o ADR como "Amended". O item saiu do `docs/BACKLOG.md` e da lista do README.
- A imagem do topo do README ainda é a antiga (`5-12.png`, com o balão flutuante). Não troquei.

**Não fiz**
- O code review com subagents que o `docs/PLAN.md` pede antes do PR.

Base directory for this skill: /home/walter/.claude/skills/code-review

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / PRD / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point — a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here — not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A PRD/spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below — a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation — and, like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name** — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code** — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy** — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps** — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession** — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches** — the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery** — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change** — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality** — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains** — long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man** — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest** — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls. Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full — the sub-agent has no other access to it.
- The brief: "Report — per file/hunk where relevant — (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings — the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes — that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

ADR 0007 and GLOSSARY were amended accordingly.

- Message Chains — long a.b().c().d() navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method.
- Middle Man — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it.
- Refused Bequest — a subclass or implementer that ignores most of what it inherits. → composition.

Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Also flag real bugs you notice in passing (e.g. the CSS width `16rem` vs the JS constant `MARGIN_CARD_WIDTH = 256` drifting, event listener leaks, dispatch during an update). Under 400 words.

# Glossary

Use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues. Avoid synonyms such as "edit", "proposal" or "patch" for a Suggestion.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Document** | The Markdown text in the editor. The only thing the app persists (`localStorage`). |
| **Block** | A top-level node of the CodeMirror Markdown syntax tree: paragraph, heading, list, blockquote, code block. A whole list is one Block. |
| **Target** | The range an AI request is about: the selection, or the Block under the cursor when nothing is selected. |
| **Neighbors** | The 2 Blocks before and the 2 after the Target, plus the document title (first `#`) and the current section heading. Sent as context. |
| **Instruction** | What the user asks for: a Quick action or free text. |
| **Quick action** | A preset Instruction: Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar. |
| **Suggestion** | A proposed replacement for a range of the Document. It lives outside the Document (an overlay) until accepted. Holds: range, original text, Replacement, Rationale, refine history. |
| **Replacement** | The new text the AI proposes for a Suggestion's range. |
| **Rationale** | One short sentence from the AI explaining the change, in the Document's language. Shown on hover, or when the cursor is inside the Suggestion; always shown on the Active Suggestion's margin card. |
| **Active Suggestion** | The one containing the cursor; otherwise the most recently asked Suggestion; otherwise the most important open Review pass Suggestion. The only one that shows the Accept / Reject / Refine card: in the right margin, level with its first line, when the window has room; otherwise floating above it. |
| **Accept** | Apply the Replacement to the Document. A normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. |
| **Reject** | Drop the Suggestion. Not undoable in v1. |
| **Refine** | A follow-up Instruction on an open Suggestion. Produces a new Replacement in place. The diff is always against the original text. |
| **Discard** | Remove a Suggestion because the user edited inside its range or a newer Suggestion overlapped it. Shows a discreet notice. |
| **Review pass** | On-demand request: the AI reads the whole Document (Blocks numbered `p1`, `p2`, …) and returns up to 6 Suggestions, one per Block, streamed one by one. |
| **Focus** | Optional free text that narrows a Review pass ("focus on tone"). |
| **Draft** | (Backlog) Streamed, not-yet-validated Replacement text shown without a diff. |
| **Bake-off** | Scripted comparison of candidate models on the same requests ([ADR 0010](docs/chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)). |
| **AI call record** | Per-call log entry for verification: task, model, provider, tokens, cost, timings, finish reason, generation id. |
| **Gate** | A point where the orchestrator stops for the maintainer's decision. |

# Chiri AI Editor

## What it is

A browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. Select text, or put the cursor in a paragraph, and ask for a change with a Quick action (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar), free text, or `⌘K`. The AI answers inline as a tracked change: the old text struck through, the new text beside it, and a one-line Rationale on hover. Small edits show a word-level diff; rewrites show the whole block. You can Accept, Reject, or Refine a Suggestion ("make it shorter", then "now more formal"). A Review pass reads the whole Document, optionally with a Focus ("tone only"), and streams up to six Suggestions, with Accept all and Reject all. Nothing touches the Document until you Accept, and Accept is a normal edit, so `⌘Z` undoes it.

![Review pass with the Focus "tone only": two word-level Suggestions and one block-level, with the toolbar on the active one](docs/chiri/verification/img/5-12.png)

**How it was built.**
- A planning session (Claude Code, `grilling` skill) produced the [ADRs](docs/chiri/adr/), the [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), the [plan](docs/PLAN.md) and six issues.
- An orchestrator session (Claude Code, `opus`) ran the six slices one after another. Each slice had a `sonnet` implementer subagent (tests first for the pure modules, then the UI), a check of the acceptance criteria in a real browser, and a review by `opus` (Standards and Spec) followed by `sonnet` until clean. The maintainer decided at three gates: the model (A), the core flow (B) and this submission (C).
- The default model, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, was chosen by a [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md) of 9 models on the same requests (final run US$0.056; about US$0.17 for the three full runs plus the language re-check; about US$0.23 for everything spent on choosing the model, with the prompt checks and probes).
- Every model call made while building was recorded against the US$5 budget in the [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md). The UI has no end-to-end suite; it was checked by hand, and each check is written up in [docs/chiri/verification/](docs/chiri/verification/).

## How to run it

Needs Node 22.12 or newer and pnpm (the version is pinned in `packageManager`; `corepack enable` installs it).

```sh
cp .env.example .env     # then set OPENROUTER_API_KEY
pnpm install
pnpm dev                 # open the printed URL
```

- `OPENROUTER_MODEL` is optional and defaults to `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`.
- The key stays on the server side. The browser sends a placeholder, and the Vite proxy (`/api/openrouter/*`) overwrites `Authorization`. `.env` is not committed and the built bundle contains no key ([ADR 0005](docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)). The app is local only; there is no hosted version.
- Without a key the app opens and shows a banner that says what is missing.
- To try it: the sample Document has an overlong paragraph, a slangy one and a typo. Select one and press `⌘K`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | Vitest. Never calls the model. |
| `pnpm biome check` | Lint and format. |
| `pnpm build` | Type-check and production build. |
| `pnpm bakeoff` | Calls the model: 9 models, 4 Quick actions and a Review pass each, about US$0.056. Rewrites `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`. Needs the key. |
| `pnpm export-sessions` | Copies the Claude Code sessions into `ai-sessions/` with OpenRouter keys masked. `--verify` compares the copy with the source. |

Keys (`Ctrl` instead of `⌘` outside macOS):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `⌘K` | Ask about the selection, or the paragraph under the cursor. Inside a Suggestion: Refine it. |
| `⌘Enter` | Accept the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `Esc` | Close the bubble or the Refine box; cancel a request or a Refine in flight; otherwise Reject the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `⌘Z` | Undo an Accept, or an Accept all in one step. Reject cannot be undone. |

## With more time

Details and sources in [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md).

1. **Version arrows for Refine** (‹ 1/3 ›). Every Refine step is already kept; only the UI is missing.
2. **Undoable Reject.** One stray `Esc` loses a Suggestion for good.
3. **A sturdier Review prompt.** In the Bake-off, moving one sentence made two models return junk Replacements. A guard drops the one shape seen so far, and the prompt still needs a Bake-off re-run after any change.
4. **A size limit for the Review pass.** It sends the whole Document, so cost and latency grow with it and nothing stops a very long one.

## Links

- [Architecture decisions](docs/chiri/adr/) (10 ADRs), [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), [plan](docs/PLAN.md)
- [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md): all 9 models side by side
- [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md): US$0.269 of 5.00 spent
- [Verification records](docs/chiri/verification/): one per slice, with screenshots and the AI call tables
- [The challenge](docs/chiri/CHALLENGE.md)
- [`ai-sessions/`](ai-sessions/): the raw Claude Code `.jsonl` files, as saved. Only OpenRouter keys are masked (`sk-or-***MASKED***`); nothing else is edited. The planning session is in the `grilling` folder. The orchestrator session is in the `chiri-implementation-orchestration` folder, and its implementer and reviewer subagents are under `<session id>/subagents/`. The orchestrator session continues after the export, so its last turns (Gate C and the merge) are not in it.

# Backlog

Reviewed at the end of slice 6, in the order I would do them. Done items are gone: the Active Suggestion no longer jumps to each new review Suggestion, and a broken answer stream has its own error text (both [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12)). Margin cards replaced the floating Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar on windows with room for them.

## Next

| Item | Why it waits | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Refine version arrows ‹ 1/3 › | The history is already kept for every step (`history`); only the UI is missing | [#11](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/11) |
| Undoable Reject (CodeMirror `invertedEffects`) | About 30 lines, but v1 accepts that a stray `Esc` loses a Suggestion. A Refine in flight or an error card already takes a first `Esc` before it Rejects | [ADR 0007](chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md), [#11](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/11) |
| Harden the Review prompt | The shipped wording passes on all 9 Bake-off models, but one sentence's position made two of them return junk Replacements. Any change needs a Bake-off re-run, about US$0.056 per full run | [#9](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/9), [bakeoff.md](chiri/bakeoff.md) |
| Junk-guard tuning | The guard drops a Replacement under 3 words for an original over 15 words (headings exempt). That covers the junk seen in the Bake-off (`x`, "Thank you!"); other shapes would pass every check | [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12), [bakeoff.md](chiri/bakeoff.md) |
| Size limit for the Review pass on huge Documents | The whole Document goes on every request: about 975 input tokens for the 331-word sample, growing in proportion. Sample-sized Documents are cheap | [ADR 0006](chiri/adr/0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md), [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12) |
| Keyboard navigation between Suggestions | Keys act on the Suggestion under the cursor, and the cards cover v1. It matters with up to 6 open Review Suggestions | [ADR 0007](chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md), [#12](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/12) |
| Rationale in the Document's language on cheaper models | `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` never slipped (0 of 9). `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` still do (6 of 9 and 3 of 9 after the ADR-faithful wording), so choosing either needs a prompt or a check first | [#9](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/pull/9), [ADR 0006](chiri/adr/0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md) |
| Model selector in the UI | `OPENROUTER_MODEL` covers v1, and the default is the Gate A choice | [ADR 0010](chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md) |
| Draft preview for Target requests | Its reopen rule has not fired: the chosen model's median Target latency is about 2.1 s, under the ~3 s line. It fires if a slower model is chosen | [ADR 0008](chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md), [bakeoff.md](chiri/bakeoff.md) |

## Out of scope, by choice

Deploy / hosted demo · proactive AI · slash commands · split-pane before/after · chat sidebar · version history · multiple documents · real-time multi-user collaboration · mobile layout · browser end-to-end tests (the UI is checked by hand, see `chiri/verification/`).

- **StrictMode double-mount:** covered. EditorPane's cleanup calls `view.destroy()`, which runs the plugin's `destroy` and disconnects the observer.
- **Layout assumption:** the main column is fixed at `max-w-3xl px-6`, so the text column is always 720px. Content-right then depends only on viewport width, which is what the observer watches.

Findings:
1. **Likely bug, `src/editor/suggestion-cards.ts:68-69`.**
   - The margin spec sets `strictSide: true` and `resize: false`. At `node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js:10605-10620` that means no flip and no height clamp.
   - A Suggestion whose first line is in the bottom ~150-200px of the viewport leaves its card, Accept/Reject included, below the fold. `scrollMargins` has no bottom margin.
   - The floating card flipped, so this is a regression.
   - Fix: drop `strictSide` from the margin spec (CodeMirror then flips above only when there is more room there). Alternatively add a bottom scroll margin. Please check this in a browser; I could only read the source.
2. **Naming violation, `docs/BACKLOG.md:19`.** The row title "Keep a Refine draft…" uses **Draft**, which GLOSSARY reserves for streamed, unvalidated Replacement text. Fix: retitle to "Keep the typed Refine Instruction when the card changes placement".
3. **`docs/BACKLOG.md:18-19`.** The Source cell says "margin cards PR" while the other rows link PRs. Fill in the link once the PR exists.
4. **`GLOSSARY.md:17`.** "The box beside a Suggestion" contradicts "floats above". Fix: "The box tied to a Suggestion".
5. **`README.md:7` and `README.md:5`.**
   - The hero alt text "floating card used before margin cards" describes history, not the image. Better to swap in `margin-cards-*.png`.
   - The intro still says "Rationale on hover".
6. **`docs/chiri/verification/img/margin-cards-1..4.png`** are untracked (so not in the diff) and nothing references them.
7. **`src/editor/suggestions.css:136-139`.** `max-width: none` does nothing for a 256px card, because the 28rem cap never applies. Remove it.

# Glossary

Use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues. Avoid synonyms such as "edit", "proposal" or "patch" for a Suggestion.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Document** | The Markdown text in the editor. The only thing the app persists (`localStorage`). |
| **Block** | A top-level node of the CodeMirror Markdown syntax tree: paragraph, heading, list, blockquote, code block. A whole list is one Block. |
| **Target** | The range an AI request is about: the selection, or the Block under the cursor when nothing is selected. |
| **Neighbors** | The 2 Blocks before and the 2 after the Target, plus the document title (first `#`) and the current section heading. Sent as context. |
| **Instruction** | What the user asks for: a Quick action or free text. |
| **Quick action** | A preset Instruction: Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar. |
| **Suggestion** | A proposed replacement for a range of the Document. It lives outside the Document (an overlay) until accepted. Holds: range, original text, Replacement, Rationale, refine history. |
| **Replacement** | The new text the AI proposes for a Suggestion's range. |
| **Rationale** | One short sentence from the AI explaining the change, in the Document's language. Shown on hover, or when the cursor is inside the Suggestion; always shown on the Active Suggestion's margin card. |
| **Active Suggestion** | The one containing the cursor; otherwise the most recently asked Suggestion; otherwise the most important open Review pass Suggestion. The only one whose Card has Accept / Reject / Refine. |
| **Card** | The box beside a Suggestion with its Rationale, plus Accept / Reject / Refine on the Active Suggestion. A margin card sits right of the text, level with the Suggestion's first line, when the window has room; otherwise the Card floats above the Suggestion. |
| **Accept** | Apply the Replacement to the Document. A normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. |
| **Reject** | Drop the Suggestion. Not undoable in v1. |
| **Refine** | A follow-up Instruction on an open Suggestion. Produces a new Replacement in place. The diff is always against the original text. |
| **Discard** | Remove a Suggestion because the user edited inside its range or a newer Suggestion overlapped it. Shows a discreet notice. |
| **Review pass** | On-demand request: the AI reads the whole Document (Blocks numbered `p1`, `p2`, …) and returns up to 6 Suggestions, one per Block, streamed one by one. |
| **Focus** | Optional free text that narrows a Review pass ("focus on tone"). |
| **Draft** | (Backlog) Streamed, not-yet-validated Replacement text shown without a diff. |
| **Bake-off** | Scripted comparison of candidate models on the same requests ([ADR 0010](docs/chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)). |
| **AI call record** | Per-call log entry for verification: task, model, provider, tokens, cost, timings, finish reason, generation id. |
| **Gate** | A point where the orchestrator stops for the maintainer's decision. |

# Chiri AI Editor

## What it is

A browser Markdown editor with an AI co-author. Select text, or put the cursor in a paragraph, and ask for a change with a Quick action (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar), free text, or `⌘K`. The AI answers inline as a tracked change: the old text struck through, the new text beside it, and a one-line Rationale on hover. Small edits show a word-level diff; rewrites show the whole block. You can Accept, Reject, or Refine a Suggestion ("make it shorter", then "now more formal"). A Review pass reads the whole Document, optionally with a Focus ("tone only"), and streams up to six Suggestions, with Accept all and Reject all. Nothing touches the Document until you Accept, and Accept is a normal edit, so `⌘Z` undoes it.

![Review pass with the Focus "tone only": two word-level Suggestions and one block-level, with the floating card used before margin cards on the active one](docs/chiri/verification/img/5-12.png)

**How it was built.**
- A planning session (Claude Code, `grilling` skill) produced the [ADRs](docs/chiri/adr/), the [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), the [plan](docs/PLAN.md) and six issues.
- An orchestrator session (Claude Code, `opus`) ran the six slices one after another. Each slice had a `sonnet` implementer subagent (tests first for the pure modules, then the UI), a check of the acceptance criteria in a real browser, and a review by `opus` (Standards and Spec) followed by `sonnet` until clean. The maintainer decided at three gates: the model (A), the core flow (B) and this submission (C).
- The default model, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, was chosen by a [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md) of 9 models on the same requests (final run US$0.056; about US$0.17 for the three full runs plus the language re-check; about US$0.23 for everything spent on choosing the model, with the prompt checks and probes).
- Every model call made while building was recorded against the US$5 budget in the [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md). The UI has no end-to-end suite; it was checked by hand, and each check is written up in [docs/chiri/verification/](docs/chiri/verification/).

## How to run it

Needs Node 22.12 or newer and pnpm (the version is pinned in `packageManager`; `corepack enable` installs it).

```sh
cp .env.example .env     # then set OPENROUTER_API_KEY
pnpm install
pnpm dev                 # open the printed URL
```

- `OPENROUTER_MODEL` is optional and defaults to `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`.
- The key stays on the server side. The browser sends a placeholder, and the Vite proxy (`/api/openrouter/*`) overwrites `Authorization`. `.env` is not committed and the built bundle contains no key ([ADR 0005](docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)). The app is local only; there is no hosted version.
- Without a key the app opens and shows a banner that says what is missing.
- To try it: the sample Document has an overlong paragraph, a slangy one and a typo. Select one and press `⌘K`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | Vitest. Never calls the model. |
| `pnpm biome check` | Lint and format. |
| `pnpm build` | Type-check and production build. |
| `pnpm bakeoff` | Calls the model: 9 models, 4 Quick actions and a Review pass each, about US$0.056. Rewrites `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`. Needs the key. |
| `pnpm export-sessions` | Copies the Claude Code sessions into `ai-sessions/` with OpenRouter keys masked. `--verify` compares the copy with the source. |

Keys (`Ctrl` instead of `⌘` outside macOS):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `⌘K` | Ask about the selection, or the paragraph under the cursor. Inside a Suggestion: Refine it. |
| `⌘Enter` | Accept the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `Esc` | Close the bubble or the Refine box; cancel a request or a Refine in flight; otherwise Reject the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `⌘Z` | Undo an Accept, or an Accept all in one step. Reject cannot be undone. |

## With more time

Details and sources in [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md).

1. **Version arrows for Refine** (‹ 1/3 ›). Every Refine step is already kept; only the UI is missing.
2. **Undoable Reject.** One stray `Esc` loses a Suggestion for good.
3. **A sturdier Review prompt.** In the Bake-off, moving one sentence made two models return junk Replacements. A guard drops the one shape seen so far, and the prompt still needs a Bake-off re-run after any change.
4. **A size limit for the Review pass.** It sends the whole Document, so cost and latency grow with it and nothing stops a very long one.

## Links

- [Architecture decisions](docs/chiri/adr/) (10 ADRs), [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), [plan](docs/PLAN.md)
- [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md): all 9 models side by side
- [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md): US$0.269 of 5.00 spent
- [Verification records](docs/chiri/verification/): one per slice, with screenshots and the AI call tables
- [The challenge](docs/chiri/CHALLENGE.md)
- [`ai-sessions/`](ai-sessions/): the raw Claude Code `.jsonl` files, as saved. Only OpenRouter keys are masked (`sk-or-***MASKED***`); nothing else is edited. The planning session is in the `grilling` folder. The orchestrator session is in the `chiri-implementation-orchestration` folder, and its implementer and reviewer subagents are under `<session id>/subagents/`. The orchestrator session continues after the export, so its last turns (Gate C and the merge) are not in it.

Nothing touches the Document until you Accept, and Accept is a normal edit, so `⌘Z` undoes it.

![Review pass with the Focus "tone only": two word-level Suggestions and one block-level, with the Accept / Reject / Refine card floating above the active one](docs/chiri/verification/img/5-12.png)

**How it was built.**
- A planning session (Claude Code, `grilling` skill) produced the [ADRs](docs/chiri/adr/), the [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), the [plan](docs/PLAN.md) and six issues.
- An orchestrator session (Claude Code, `opus`) ran the six slices one after another. Each slice had a `sonnet` implementer subagent (tests first for the pure modules, then the UI), a check of the acceptance criteria in a real browser, and a review by `opus` (Standards and Spec) followed by `sonnet` until clean. The maintainer decided at three gates: the model (A), the core flow (B) and this submission (C).
- The default model, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, was chosen by a [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md) of 9 models on the same requests (final run US$0.056; about US$0.17 for the three full runs plus the language re-check; about US$0.23 for everything spent on choosing the model, with the prompt checks and probes).
- Every model call made while building was recorded against the US$5 budget in the [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md). The UI has no end-to-end suite; it was checked by hand, and each check is written up in [docs/chiri/verification/](docs/chiri/verification/).

## How to run it

Needs Node 22.12 or newer and pnpm (the version is pinned in `packageManager`; `corepack enable` installs it).

```sh
cp .env.example .env     # then set OPENROUTER_API_KEY
pnpm install
pnpm dev                 # open the printed URL
```

- `OPENROUTER_MODEL` is optional and defaults to `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`.
- The key stays on the server side. The browser sends a placeholder, and the Vite proxy (`/api/openrouter/*`) overwrites `Authorization`. `.env` is not committed and the built bundle contains no key ([ADR 0005](docs/chiri/adr/0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)). The app is local only; there is no hosted version.
- Without a key the app opens and shows a banner that says what is missing.
- To try it: the sample Document has an overlong paragraph, a slangy one and a typo. Select one and press `⌘K`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | Vitest. Never calls the model. |
| `pnpm biome check` | Lint and format. |
| `pnpm build` | Type-check and production build. |
| `pnpm bakeoff` | Calls the model: 9 models, 4 Quick actions and a Review pass each, about US$0.056. Rewrites `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`. Needs the key. |
| `pnpm export-sessions` | Copies the Claude Code sessions into `ai-sessions/` with OpenRouter keys masked. `--verify` compares the copy with the source. |

Keys (`Ctrl` instead of `⌘` outside macOS):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `⌘K` | Ask about the selection, or the paragraph under the cursor. Inside a Suggestion: Refine it. |
| `⌘Enter` | Accept the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `Esc` | Close the bubble or the Refine box; cancel a request or a Refine in flight; otherwise Reject the Suggestion under the cursor. |
| `⌘Z` | Undo an Accept, or an Accept all in one step. Reject cannot be undone. |

## With more time

Details and sources in [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md).

1. **Version arrows for Refine** (‹ 1/3 ›). Every Refine step is already kept; only the UI is missing.
2. **Undoable Reject.** One stray `Esc` loses a Suggestion for good.
3. **A sturdier Review prompt.** In the Bake-off, moving one sentence made two models return junk Replacements. A guard drops the one shape seen so far, and the prompt still needs a Bake-off re-run after any change.
4. **A size limit for the Review pass.** It sends the whole Document, so cost and latency grow with it and nothing stops a very long one.

## Links

- [Architecture decisions](docs/chiri/adr/) (10 ADRs), [glossary](GLOSSARY.md), [plan](docs/PLAN.md)
- [Bake-off](docs/chiri/bakeoff.md): all 9 models side by side
- [AI cost log](docs/chiri/ai-costs.md): US$0.269 of 5.00 spent
- [Verification records](docs/chiri/verification/): one per slice, with screenshots and the AI call tables
- [The challenge](docs/chiri/CHALLENGE.md)
- [`ai-sessions/`](ai-sessions/): the raw Claude Code `.jsonl` files, as saved. Only OpenRouter keys are masked (`sk-or-***MASKED***`); nothing else is edited. The planning session is in the `grilling` folder. The orchestrator session is in the `chiri-implementation-orchestration` folder, and its implementer and reviewer subagents are under `<session id>/subagents/`. The orchestrator session continues after the export, so its last turns (Gate C and the merge) are not in it.

O review rodou em duas passadas e corrigi o que era real. Nada foi commitado ainda.

**O que mudou por causa do review**
- **Largura do cartão:** agora vem só do JS (`MARGIN_CARD_WIDTH`, aplicada direto no elemento). Antes, o CSS dizia `16rem` e o JS dizia `256`. Os dois só batiam com a fonte padrão de 16px.
- **Modo velho:** um `ResizeObserver` no `documentElement` agora decide entre margem e balão. Ele percebe resize da janela e também a barra de rolagem aparecendo ou sumindo. Testei no browser: com a janela fixa em 1320px, esconder a barra vira `margin`, e ela voltar vira `floating`.
- **Os 3 `if` de modo:** viraram uma tabela só, `placements`, em [suggestion-cards.ts](src/editor/suggestion-cards.ts). Ela guarda o lado, a largura, se o Rationale fica sempre visível e como posicionar.
- **`viewportOf`:** agora é reaproveitado de [tooltip-space.ts](src/editor/tooltip-space.ts) em vez de copiado.
- **Docs:**
  - o Glossary ganhou a linha **Card**;
  - o texto alternativo e a introdução do README falam do cartão;
  - um título no backlog usava "Draft", que no Glossary quer dizer outra coisa, e foi trocado.
- Testes: 639 passando (um teste repetido virou um só). Biome e build verdes.

**O que ficou de fora de propósito (anotado no `docs/BACKLOG.md`)**
- **Bordas da tela.** O cartão fica preso na primeira linha da Suggestion, sempre do mesmo lado. Por isso ele some junto quando essa linha entra embaixo do header. E perto do rodapé, os botões ficam abaixo da borda da tela até você rolar. O segundo revisor chamou isso de regressão, porque o balão antigo virava para cima nesse caso. Mantive assim porque, sem a trava, o cartão vira e continua desalinhado da linha depois que você rola. Isso tirei do código do CodeMirror, sem testar no browser.
- **Texto do Refine.** Se você redimensionar a janela cruzando os ~1312px enquanto digita no Refine, o texto digitado some.
- **Ask bubble.** Se ela invade a margem, o cartão desce para baixo dela enquanto ela está aberta. Deixei assim: quem cede lugar é o cartão, não a bolha que você está usando.

**Falta**
- Commit, PR, os prints `margin-cards-1..4.png` no PR, e o link do PR nas duas linhas novas do backlog.

content.text:
Não consigo ver o seu browser daqui, então preciso que você rode um comando.

O app guarda dois registros em modo dev:
- `window.__aiCalls`: cada chamada à IA, com custo, tokens e por que ela parou.
- `window.__reviewDrops`: cada Suggestion que a IA mandou e o app jogou fora, com o motivo. Os motivos possíveis são `unchanged` (nada mudou), `junk` (resposta curta demais), `code-block` (bloco de código), `occupied` (o bloco já tinha uma Suggestion), `unknown-block`, `duplicate-block`, `empty`, `over-limit` e `text-changed`.

Cole isto no console da aba do Chiri:

```js
copy(JSON.stringify({ drops: window.__reviewDrops ?? [], calls: window.__aiCalls ?? [] }, null, 2))
```

Isso copia os dois registros para a área de transferência. É só colar aqui. Não tem chave nem segredo ali dentro, só números, o modelo e o motivo de cada descarte.

- **Se `drops` vier vazio:** a IA propôs uma só. Num texto técnico como esse, com um Focus de tom, isso é plausível.
- **Se vier cheio:** o app descartou Suggestions boas. Aí é bug no guard, e eu investigo.

**Uma coisa que o seu print mostra, à parte:** o cartão está na altura de "Repository:", duas linhas acima da primeira mudança ("Critical → Important"). Isso segue a regra combinada, porque a Suggestion cobre o bloco inteiro. Sem linha em branco entre elas, "Repository", "Documentation" e "Critical" formam um só bloco, e o cartão se alinha com o começo dele. Se você preferir o cartão na altura da **primeira palavra que muda**, dá para fazer. O preço é que, num bloco reescrito do zero, as duas posições são iguais, e numa troca pequena no fim de um parágrafo longo o cartão fica longe do topo do bloco.

O app não jogou nada fora: `drops` veio vazio. Quem decidiu quantas Suggestions mandar foi a IA. Dá para ver pelo tamanho de cada resposta:

| Review | Focus | Tokens de saída | O que isso indica |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1ª | "Shorten the Description" | 198 | ~1 Suggestion |
| 2ª | "Tone" | 120 | 1 Suggestion (a do "Critical → Important") |
| 3ª | "concision" | 792 | várias, provavelmente 3 a 5 |

Na terceira, você viu 2 no print. As outras devem estar mais abaixo, fora da tela.

Dois motivos explicam o número baixo, e nenhum é bug:

1. **O Focus estreita.** "Tone" num texto técnico neutro deixa pouco para mudar.
2. **O texto colado tem poucos blocos.** A Review propõe no máximo uma Suggestion por bloco. Como as linhas estão separadas por quebra simples, sem linha em branco, parágrafos inteiros viram um bloco só. Pelo print, o documento todo tem uns 6 a 8 blocos, e alguns são enormes. O teto de 6 quase não tem por onde subir. Isso eu deduzi do print, não contei no código.

**Custo dos seus testes:** US$0.0134 no total (1 Shorter e 3 Reviews). Vou registrar isso no `docs/chiri/ai-costs.md` junto com o PR, como o AGENTS.md pede.

Esse mesmo formato de texto colado é o que joga o cartão para longe da mudança, como no seu print anterior. Ainda espero sua resposta: alinho o cartão com a **primeira mudança visível** ou deixo no **começo do bloco**?

# AI costs

Budget: US$5.00, the cap on the OpenRouter key. Every Bake-off run and every verification check that calls a model adds rows here (format in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#ai-call-records)). Claude Code usage while building is not billed to this key and is not tracked here.

| Date | Slice / PR | Task | Model → served by | Tokens in / out / reasoning / cached | Cost (US$) | Latency client / OpenRouter / generation (ms) | Finish | Valid | Record |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-28 | #2 | Bake-off: 4 Quick actions + Review pass | `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` → Cohere, InferenceNet, DigitalOcean | 2495 / 1002 / 258 / 384 | 0.000770 | 1731 / 3221 (median Target / Review) | stop ×5 | 5/5, no retries | [bakeoff.md](bakeoff.md) |
| 2026-10-28 | #2 | Bake-off: 4 Quick actions + Review pass | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` → AtlasCloud, Fireworks, Relace, PrimeIntellect | 3062 / 1853 / 1107 / 1910 | 0.001853 | 2108 / 5078 (median Target / Review) | stop ×5 | 5/5, no retries | [bakeoff.md](bakeoff.md) |
| 2026-10-28 | #2 | Bake-off: 4 Quick actions + Review pass | `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` → Alibaba | 1867 / 2806 / 2451 / 1536 | 0.001393 | 13643 / – (median Target / Review) | stop ×4 | 4/5, no retries | [bakeoff.md](bakeoff.md) |
| 2026-10-28 | #2 | Bake-off: 4 Quick actions + Review pass | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` → Google | 3201 / 544 / 0 / 0 | 0.002320 | 1813 / 2183 (median Target / Review) | stop ×5 | 5/5, no retries | [bakeoff.md](bakeoff.md) |
| 2026-10-28 | #2 | Bake-off: 4 Quick actions + Review pass | `google/gemini-3.8-flash` → Google | 3201 / 1204 / 504 / 0 | 0.006916 | 5379 / 6451 (median Target / Review) | stop ×5 | 5/5, no retries | [bakeoff.md](bakeoff.md) |
| 2026-10-28 | #2 | Bake-off: 4 Quick actions + Review pass | `google/gemini-4-argon` → Google AI Studio, Google | 3894 / 715 / 0 / 0 | 0.014938 | 10305 / 7973 (median Target / Review) | stop ×5 | 5/5, no retries | [bakeoff.md](bakeoff.md) |
...

Notes on slice 5:
- Slice cost is about US$0.0137 recorded: 5 Review passes at US$0.0016 to US$0.0027, 1 Refine and 1 Quick action. The Stopped pass was aborted before the answer was complete and OpenRouter reported no usage for it, so it is not in the sum; a whole pass costs about US$0.0026. The failures were stubs and never reached OpenRouter. The slice budget was US$0.06.
- A Review pass on the 13-Block sample Document sends about 975 tokens, against about 520 for a Target request, because the whole Document goes in.

Notes on slice 6:
- No model calls. The fresh-clone check only used `GET /models` and `GET /auth/key` through the proxy, which are not generations and cost nothing.
- The counter is the lifetime usage of the key, so US$0.269 is an upper bound for this project. It agrees with the rows within the unreported aborted requests (the Stopped pass of slice 5 and the aborted requests of slices 3 and 4).
Closes #
